claims.text: gate_candidates -- added here so this wrapper does not silently strip a capability that module already supports; see that function's own docstring for exactly what it covers (every TaskAttempt in this batch) and does not (the cumulative re-gate inside promote_candidates, a separate, filed follow-up, not this method's concern since it never promotes).

claims.why: The claim about gate_candidates' coverage and promote_candidates cannot be verified without the docstring of gate_candidates and the implementation of promote_candidates, neither present in this chunk.

claims.text: Landing a candidate this returns into repo_root is a SEPARATE, explicit act -- see gate_candidates and promote_candidates and the comment on can_parallel in dispatch for why this method does not do that itself.
claims.where: docstring of gate_concurrent_writes (lines before line 281, referenced by code)
claims.why: The claim references promote_candidates and a comment on can_parallel in dispatch, neither of which are in this chunk; the claim about the method not doing the landing itself is consistent with the code (gate_concurrent_writes returns a list, no promotion logic), but the full verification requires external code.

claims.text: One-shot entry: decompose a single objective into subtasks, then plan (dry_run) or dispatch (live) them across the bounded local bench.
claims.why: spawn calls decompose, then either plan (if dry_run) or dispatch (if not dry_run).

claims.text: This is the dynamic counterpart to the hardcoded _demo_tasks flow -- the subtasks come from decompose (local model with a deterministic per-path fallback), not a fixed list.
claims.why: The claim about decompose's behavior (local model with deterministic per-path fallback) cannot be verified without the decompose function's implementation, not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Dynamic agent configurator: mint or reshape an agent-role definition at runtime. Ikarus owns the crew roster, so creating/editing roles is his job -- routing (router.load_agents) picks up the change with no restart. Returns a summary; raises ValueError on an invalid spec.
claims.why: The claim about Ikarus ownership, router.load_agents picking up changes, and raising ValueError on invalid spec cannot be verified without the agents_registry module and the router module, not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Returns a summary; raises ValueError on an invalid spec.
claims.why: The code in configure does not raise ValueError; it calls reg.get_role and reg.update_role or reg.create_role, but there is no try/except or explicit raise for invalid spec. If the spec is invalid, the registry functions may raise other exceptions, but the docstring specifically promises ValueError, which is not implemented.
